review.alternative: Deterministic abstentions might still yield useful heuristic bounds without satisfying strict stochastic identifiability.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical demonstration that deterministic abstention models consistently outperform stochastic ones in counterfactual score recovery.

claims.statement: Abstaining classifiers permit counterfactual score identification under stochastic abstentions and independent evaluation data.

support.explanation: Defines the exact identifiability criteria for counterfactual performance evaluation of abstentions.
support.passage: We specify the conditions under which the counterfactual score is identifiable: if the abstentions are stochastic, and if the evaluation data is independent of the training data (ensuring that the predictions are missing at random), then the score is identifiable.

actions.findings: Abstaining classifiers permit counterfactual score identification under stochastic abstentions and independent evaluation data. [source-b3c814c088724721]
actions.limitations: Analysis is restricted to available theoretical frameworks on abstention and counterfactual identification; direct empirical tests on live large-scale multi-turn reasoning models remain limited.
actions.next_questions: How can nonparametric doubly robust estimators be adapted to runtime self-correction loops in autonomous reasoning agents?
actions.reason: The project proj-assumption-falsification is synthesis-ready and requires a structured notebook connecting collected evidence on counterfactual scoring and cognitive augmentation to the question of automated premise correction.
actions.summary: We examine the identification conditions of counterfactual scores for abstaining classifiers and their implications for detecting incorrect foundational premises in automated reasoning systems.
actions.title: Analysis of Counterfactual Scoring and Foundational Reasoning Limits
